key_insight: Geometry-based fragmentation creates adjustable, multiscale molecular representations without predefined chemical fragmentation rules for polymer property prediction.
engineering_relevance: Combining polymer sequence representations with 3D fragment information can improve prediction of properties influenced by molecular structure at different scales.
method: Partition structures using a radius-constrained optimization inspired by k-center clustering.
Vary the radius to control fragment size and construct multiscale representations.
Integrate geometric fragment attention with p-SMILES and 3D conformational information.
evidence_signal: On a benchmark polymer dataset, adding 3D conformational information improved accuracy for several properties over p-SMILES-only models; explainability analyses explored the physical relevance of learned representations.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify accuracy gains or establish robustness to conformer selection and unfamiliar polymer chemistries.
paper_title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
